summary: Two findings, ranked. The boundary write is the one that matters if real; the index counter is lower consequence.

findings.title: Page loop writes one past the caller's buffer
findings.mechanism: The loop bound is <= pageSize, so on any page with more than pageSize items remaining Paginate appends pageSize+1 items; the caller in listPage checks len(page) > pageSize and panics, so a full page crashes the process.

recommended_validation.description: A table test calling Paginate with pageSize items for pageSize in 1..5 and asserting the result length equals pageSize and no panic occurs.

findings.uncertainty: Have not confirmed whether any caller other than listPage tolerates an oversize page.

findings.title: Paginate returns nil rather than an empty page at the end of the list
findings.mechanism: When offset equals len(items) Paginate returns nil instead of an empty slice, so a caller that distinguishes nil from empty treats the final page as an error rather than as end-of-list.

recommended_validation.description: Call Paginate with offset == len(items) and assert the result is non-nil and empty.
